title: "Thy Kingdom Come!" the Heathen Lands
description: "Thy Kingdom Come!" the Heathen Lands in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Emily Taylor wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 171, “Thy Kingdom Come!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Thy king-dom come!" The hea-then lands, In er-ror sunk, Thy pre-sence crave; And vic-tims bound by ty-rant hands Im-plore Thee, Fa-ther, come and save!

lines: In error sunk, Thy presence crave;
And victims bound by tyrant hands
Implore Thee, Father, come and save!
In doubt and darkness calls for Thee;
For Thou hast eyes to give the blind,
And strength to set the captive free.
Thy reign of peace and love begin!
Too oft the Christian's sacred name
Is stained by wrath and shamed by sin;
O, come, assert the gospel's claim!
O, never in that righteous cause
Our hearts be slow, our voices dumb;
Upon the glorious theme we pause,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Emily Taylor died in 1872.
credits: Words by Emily Taylor (1795–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
